title: Five equations for first-order logic, modulo the structure of existential graphs
summary: Peirce’s existential graphs draw a first-order formula so that the order and grouping of conjuncts, the names and order of bound variables, the position of a quantifier relative to conjuncts that do not mention its variable, and how a network of equalities is written cannot be seen. We take these structural laws for granted. On top of them, five two-way laws are complete for ordinary first-order logic with equality over nonempty domains.
